chapter: Chicago in the 1920s: Bix, Armstrong, Morton
title: Violinists Paul Dominguez and Armand Piron compared
summary: Howard knew Dominguez and Piron and says their violin playing was more embellished variations than his own.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: Sure. Did you know him? Sure, very well. Now how would his playing compare with your playing at that time? You mean violin? Yeah.
Oh well I think he played more saxophone than he did violin. He played, I think it was ten saxophone. I mean the way he played violin.
Was it the same approach to the instrument? No. Well how was it different?

I can't answer that because it's been too long, honestly. I mean it is not the one answer, I just don't remember, that's a long time of course. He's speaking about 1922. Piron, I remember him very well too. Did you know Piron? Very well. Was he a good violin player? Yeah. But I mean they didn't play any too hard, they played variations, you know what I mean, the oblicatas, you know. Did you play violin the same way you played clarinet? Use the same ideas and the same? Yeah. I do now. You do now. Listen I got a little bit of technique on fiddle. Huh? I got a little bit of technique on fiddle.
